description: Given an Airflow DAG that shells out or runs containers (non-dbt) via BashOperator, SSHOperator, or KubernetesPodOperator, map each to the matching Orchestra integration (PYTHON, LINUX_SSH/WINDOWS_SSH, or AWS_EKS/GKE/AKS) and produce valid pipeline YAML.

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG that uses BashOperator to run a Python script into an equivalent Orchestra pipeline task (see files/bash_python_script.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON task running PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT whose command parameter is the flattened 'cd /opt/airflow && python scripts/transform_customers.py --env prod' string, with python_version and package_manager set and a connection reference — not a LINUX_SSH task.

assertions.text: The task uses the PYTHON integration
The task runs the PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT job
The command references the source script
integration_job only ever takes a valid PYTHON value
bash_command is not carried over verbatim as a LINUX_SSH command — a BashOperator running a Python script maps to PYTHON, never LINUX_SSH
python_version and package_manager are populated with sensible defaults (e.g. '3.12' / PIP) since BashOperator's bash_command has no equivalent fields to carry over literally

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG that uses SSHOperator to run a genuine remote shell command on a Linux host into an equivalent Orchestra pipeline task (see files/ssh_remote_sync.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live SSH access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A LINUX_SSH task running LINUX_SSH_EXECUTE_COMMAND with parameters.command set to the exact remote shell command, and a connection reference standing in for ssh_conn_id rather than any host/username/key material being inlined.

assertions.text: The task uses the LINUX_SSH integration
The task runs the LINUX_SSH_EXECUTE_COMMAND job
The command references the remote sync script
integration_job only ever takes a valid LINUX_SSH value
ssh_conn_id (etl_box) is not written into the YAML as a literal parameter value — it is represented purely by the connection: reference
parameters contains only command, matching LINUX_SSH_EXECUTE_COMMAND's parameter model — no invented host/user/key fields are added alongside it

evals.prompt: Convert this Airflow DAG that uses KubernetesPodOperator to run a containerised enrichment job on an AWS EKS cluster into an equivalent Orchestra pipeline task (see files/k8s_pod_enrichment.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live AWS access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An AWS_EKS task running AWS_EKS_RUN_JOB whose job_manifest carries over the container image, namespace, and env vars from the KubernetesPodOperator, connecting via a named AWS connection rather than launching an arbitrary image outside a job manifest.

assertions.text: The task uses the AWS_EKS integration
The task runs the AWS_EKS_RUN_JOB job
The job name/image from the source is carried over
integration_job only ever takes a valid AWS_EKS value
The image (123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/enrichment:latest), namespace (data-team), and env_vars (ENV=prod) are reflected in the job_manifest rather than invented or dropped

cluster_context and any AWS credential material are not inlined as literal parameter values — the AWS connection reference stands in for them, and this is represented as running a job manifest (AWS_EKS_RUN_JOB), not as launching an arbitrary image directly
